headline: What to Do If You're Accused of a State Crime

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
Being accused of a state crime, whether it's a misdemeanor or a felony, can be incredibly stressful and confusing. It's natural to feel overwhelmed, but knowing the right steps to take immediately can make a huge difference in protecting your future. Here's a quick guide.

First, and this is non-negotiable, remain silent. You have the right to an attorney, so use it. Don't answer questions or offer explanations to law enforcement without your lawyer present. Anything you say can be used against you, even if you think you're just being cooperative.

Second, don't resist arrest, even if you believe it's unlawful. Resisting can lead to additional charges. Cooperate physically, but verbally assert your right to remain silent and to speak with an attorney.

Third, contact a state criminal defense lawyer as soon as humanly possible. An attorney like Angelo Reyes, who serves San Diego County and surrounding areas, can step in immediately to advise you on your rights, review the charges, and start building your defense. Early intervention can be crucial for outcomes like bail, evidence gathering, and initial court appearances.

Finally, avoid discussing your case with anyone other than your attorney. This includes friends, family, or on social media. Loose lips can sink ships, especially when your freedom is on the line.
